name: Halo
author: Erin Carter
description: Snell's window seen from underwater: one bright wavering disc of surface light hangs high in the frame, its interior a soft warm-to-cool palette blend brightest at centre, like sky read through a heaving surface. The rim frays with ridged noise into filamental tongues where total internal reflection breaks, and outside it the field falls quickly into deep blue-black. The fray crawls slowly around the disc, the radius breathes, and the interior shimmers — all very slow, nothing that resets.

params.label: Halo radius
params.effect: CSS-pixel radius of the Snell's-window disc, from a distant porthole to a frame-filling ceiling of light.

params.label: Fray depth
params.effect: Depth of the rim's ridged-noise fraying — 0 leaves a clean breathing circle, 2 tears long filamental tongues from the edge.

params.label: Waver speed
params.effect: How fast the rim fray crawls around the disc and the interior shimmer rolls.
